ZH.Who — Round 1, Two Directions

Twenty options in crimson, ten per direction. Cards 01–10 are the Need for Speed: Underground 2 read — early-2000s import-tuner lettering, wide and heavy and usually oblique, the language of body-kit decals and boost gauges. Cards 11–20 are cyberpunk, deliberately spread across its sub-flavours rather than ten of one idea: Cyberpunk 2077 chamfer, Blade Runner geometric, terminal mono, pixel, glitch, and neon tube. Z, H and W each toggle case independently — eight combinations per option, switchable above. Every font is SIL Open Font License, free for commercial merchandise. Colours come from sh2.store.

The closest free stand-in for Eurostile Bold Extended Oblique — which is the face that actually was on mid-2000s racing HUDs and decal sheets. If one option here is literally the NFSU2 answer, it is this one.

Production files are in this folder as NN-slug.svg. They are plain outlined SVG — open in Illustrator, Inkscape, Affinity or Cricut Design Space, or hand them to a printer as-is. Each file holds exactly two paths, one gold and one red, so colour separation is already done.

The keyline toggle previews a bone-coloured sticker border. Most print shops generate the actual die-cut contour themselves from the artwork outline, so send the flat files unless yours asks for a cut path.
